title: Public library: Sunday opening and shorter weekday evenings
question: What could happen if the Ostrand public library opens on Sundays and closes on two weekday evenings?

documents.name: 01-service-review.md
documents.content:
# Ostrand Library Service: review of opening hours

This is a fictional review written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Hours today

The central library opens from 9am to 7pm on Monday to Thursday, 9am to 5pm on Friday and 10am to 2pm on Saturday, which is 52 hours a week, and is closed on Sunday. Two branch libraries open 10am to 6pm on weekdays only.

## Use by time of day

Visit counts for last year show that Tuesday and Wednesday evenings after 5pm account for 7% of weekly visits to the central library, and that Saturday is the busiest day. Students use the study rooms most in the evenings.

## The proposal

The review proposes opening the central library from noon to 4pm on Sundays and closing it at 5pm on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Branch libraries would not change.

## Not yet decided

The review does not say how many extra staff hours a Sunday opening would need, and nobody has priced the cost.

documents.name: 02-staff-and-facilities-note.md
documents.content:
# Staff and facilities note

This is a fictional note written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Staffing

The library employs 22 staff, of whom 14 work at the central library. Sunday work is voluntary under the staff agreement and is paid at 1.5 times the normal rate. The staff union asks for two weeks' notice of any rota change, and the agreement says no one may be rostered for more than five days in a row.

## Statutory duty

The County Library Standard says that every central library must be open at least 50 hours a week. Closing two evenings at 5pm would take the central library to 48 hours unless Sunday hours are added.

## Building and contracts

The cleaning contract covers six days a week and would need a variation to cover Sunday. The building has a single lift, and the lift engineer is not on call at weekends.

## Budget

The annual library budget is fixed by the council and may not be exceeded. A modest saving of about £9,000 a year is expected from shorter weekday evenings.

documents.name: 03-community-feedback.md
documents.content:
# Community feedback summary

This is a fictional summary written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Who answered

The library asked users in March, and 640 people replied. Replies came mostly from adults who visit at least once a week. Children, and people who do not use the library, were not asked.

## What people said

- 58% said they would use Sunday opening at least once a month.
- 21% said they rely on the Tuesday and Wednesday evenings and would be hurt by an earlier closing.
- Parents asked for Sunday opening for children's reading groups.
- Students said the study rooms are full on weekday evenings and asked for them to stay open.
- Older users asked for the step-free entrance to remain staffed during all opening hours.

## Other points

The branch survey reports that Tuesday and Wednesday evenings after 5pm account for 12% of weekly visits to the central library. A local community radio station has said it will cover the change. People without home internet use the library computers, and the survey did not ask how many.
